content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to Matthew 1:20 because the parties gave two different readings of that verse, which invokes the rule governing verses with two senses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase A verse that carries two senses at once is not open had to be read either as allowing UNDERDETERMINED when two readings are offered, or as requiring both senses to stand rather than leaving the matter open.","why":"The judge used the two competing senses of Matthew 1:20 as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, but the rule says such a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand."}
